C-SEARCH-LIFECYCLE-DISCARD.Name: Search lifecycle cancellation identity — implementation plan
C-SEARCH-LIFECYCLE-DISCARD.IntentSummary: Make cancellation an identity check on every asynchronous answer of the search-and-workspace zone, with no backend edits: the project-search store claims its search generation exactly once per runSearch invocation — ahead of every early return — so clearing the keyword, losing the roots or an invalid max file size can no longer be overwritten by a prior generation's completion; the two unreachable didSearchPaths wire limits (the store's "Showing first 100 results only", quickOpen's ">30 files" cancel — the wire never delivers the event) are deleted, and the store replaces the 100 promise with an honest delivered-match cap (named constant SEARCH_RESULT_CAP = 100, counted on the grouped envelopes' matches summed, the crossing envelope sliced to the exact remaining count, the walk cancelled through the existing raw-promise cancel seam, the set marked partial through the existing #303 partialResults state so the existing localized notice renders, error kept empty — a cap is not a failure); quick open's unload cancels the in-flight debounce or searcher walk through the existing _cancelFn seam while still clearing subcommands; the command palette guards updateCommands writes with a monotonic request sequence (the linkPathPicker precedent) so a superseded resolution or rejection touches nothing and the newest request solely owns the list, with searcherBusy reset on dialog close because unload now really cancels; the muya image path hints capture a sequence number around the imagePathAutoComplete await and drop stale muya-image-picker dispatches; and a folder close that races the watcher subscription cannot leak the renderer listener (per-subscription monotonic token, the late .then re-checks identity, self-disposes and stores nothing for a closed root, and the token map is cleaned on CLOSE_PROJECT). The three mock-fed pins of dead behavior are documented replacements, not silent weakenings. Shim production source, src-tauri, i18n and the dead typed facade stay read-only.
C-SEARCH-LIFECYCLE-DISCARD.ReferenceState: Authored 2026-11-23 as a draft against the current read-only state of the green-search2 worktree (branch spec/search-lifecycle-discard, base 689df8aa); this plan names the spec by the Spec element and pins no SpecSha256 until admission. Verified defect shapes in the current tree: src/renderer/src/store/search.js claims the generation only at the real spawn ("const generation = ++this._searchGeneration", :178) while the early returns sit above it — empty roots (:141-148), the cancel line (:149), the error/partial reset (:150-152) and the empty-keyword clear (:153-157) — so a cancelled searcher's resolve-triggered .then passes the stale guard (:220) and writes the outdated collected set over the just-cleared results (outerPromise.cancel sends mt::search-cancel and settles with resolve, src/renderer/src/node/ripgrepSearcher.js:110-113); the dead limit branch (:196-202) waits for a searchedPaths event that the wire never emits (the shim's mt::search-event translation branch handles exactly match/complete/cancelled/error, src/renderer/src/_shims/install-window-globals.js:395-427, and the string "searchedPaths" appears nowhere in the shim) and would write hardcoded English into this.error — the #303 failure voice. commands/quickOpen.js: unload (:78-80) only clears subcommands although the palette's close path calls it (handleDialogClose, components/commandPalette/index.vue:121-130), and the dead didSearchPaths branch (:139-147) carries the ">30 files" promise; updateCommands (:215-249) writes availableCommands/searcherBusy/selectedCommandIndex from whichever search resolution lands last with no query identity, so a superseded traversal briefly flashes its partial list; its catch (:228-236) keeps the existing silence for message-less rejections ("The query was cancel or restarted if `message` is null.") — and the deep suite pins that silence (tests/renderer/components/commandPalette-deep.test.js :439-459, searcherBusy stays true for a current-request message-null rejection), which this plan preserves byte-for-byte. src/muya/lib/ui/imageSelector/index.js handleKeyUp (:136-175) awaits imagePathAutoComplete and dispatches muya-image-picker with no race guard, while the link flavor fixed the same defect with a sequence guard (src/muya/lib/ui/linkPathPicker/index.js :151-158, insertPath bumps _seq at :171). store/project.js: ADD_PROJECT's subscribe .then (:385-396) stores the disposer unconditionally into the module-level watchDisposers Map (:93) while CLOSE_PROJECT (:814-824) disposes only what is already stored — a close racing the subscribe leaks the renderer listener and a stale entry can overwrite a re-opened root's disposer. The delay() canceller rejects with NO argument (src/renderer/src/util/index.js :16, rejectFn()) — the factual cancel-rejection shape is the value undefined, not a message-null object. Tests: the mock-fed pins live at tests/renderer/store/search.test.ts :228-261 ("canceling on >100 paths sets error message", with the outdated source-bug comment), tests/renderer/store/search-coverage.test.js :230-252 ("didSearchPaths under 100 does not set error") and tests/renderer/commands/quickOpen-deep.test.js (:215 calling options.didSearchPaths(1), :242 "didSearchPaths sets canceled flag (< 30 does not cancel)", :282-296 calling options.didSearchPaths(2)), plus the file header line 13 describing the dead branch. Recorded plan choices (review minors): (a) tests pin the factual undefined cancel-rejection form of delay() — the palette silence guard "error && error.message" treats undefined and the historical message-null form identically, and the existing current-request silence pin stays untouched; (b) cap granularity is EXACT truncation — the grouped envelope that crosses the cap is sliced so the displayed match count equals SEARCH_RESULT_CAP precisely (the number the overlay's summary reports); dropping whole files would undershoot the promise's number and misreport, and a zero-match entry is never emitted; (c) the subscription-identity token map is itself cleaned on CLOSE_PROJECT (entry deleted together with the disposer entry) — the leak pattern is not reproduced; identity uses ONE module-level monotonic counter (never reset per root) so a closed-and-reopened root cannot collide with a stale in-flight subscription; (d) the quickOpen-deep header line 13 is rewritten with the dead-branch description. Baseline divergence: this specification is authored against a base WITHOUT the sibling C-SEARCH-RESULT-CONTRACT (#320, approved in the green-search1 worktree); this plan executes on the current base and lands on top of #320 — before the PR the orchestrator rebases/merges onto #320's delivery state and reruns its suites (list in Environment); #320 edits quickOpen.js's didMatch consumer, the shim's honest range form and the projectSearch/searchResultItem keyboard surfaces, all disjoint from this plan's regions, and line anchors in this plan are pre-rebase references re-resolved against the delivery baseline in T-003. Approval of the spec alone does not approve this plan, execution, apply/archive or release.

T-001.Title: Failing-first store pins: stale-clear discard, honest delivered-match cap, documented replacement of the two mock-fed didSearchPaths pins

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: tests/renderer/store/search.test.ts gains the failing-first pin "clearing the keyword while a search is running does not bring the old matches back" on the existing harness (searchSpy behind the FakeRipgrepDirectorySearcher mock, projectStateProxy/preferencesProxy): a controlled deferred thenable (resolve under test control, cancel vi.fn()) with opts.didMatch captured; matches are delivered, the keyword is cleared while the search runs (SET_KEYWORD('')), the mock's promise then resolves — and results stay empty, running stays false, partialResults stays false, and the generation-1 cancel was invoked exactly once (by the supersede path) with no further cancel after settle; the same discard is pinned for the other early-return paths (no opened roots, invalid max file size) and for a superseding keystroke. Today the stale completion rewrites the cleared results because the generation claim sits at :178 below the early returns — the test is red before the fix; the two existing generation-guard suites stay green.

Failing-first delivered-match cap test replacing "canceling on >100 paths sets error message" (:228-261, including its outdated source-bug comment): a searcher mock delivers more than the cap in grouped envelopes ({ filePath, matches }) — delivered asynchronously one microtask after search() returns, the real wire shape (the source's cancel seam closes over the raw promise, so synchronous delivery would hit the documented temporal dead zone the old pin's comment describes) — e.g. 40 + 40 + 40 matches; end state: the displayed set sums to exactly 100 delivered matches (the matchCount unit), the crossing envelope is sliced to the exact remaining count with no zero-match entry emitted, partialResults is true (the overlay's existing partial notice renders from it), running is false, the raw promise's cancel was invoked once, and the error state stays '' — a cap is not a failure; a subsequent keystroke clears the partial state; the cap fires on real didMatch deliveries, not on a synthetic path-count callback, and does not depend on the backend terminal's partial flag.

Documented replacement of the third mock-fed pin: tests/renderer/store/search-coverage.test.js "didSearchPaths under 100 does not set error" (:230-252), which captures opts.didSearchPaths from the store and calls it, is rewritten to pin the removed option alongside the others — the captured third options argument has didSearchPaths undefined, the error state stays '' and no cancel was invoked; both replaced store pins stay named in this change's record (ReferenceState and T-002/T-003).

T-002.Title: Store implementation: one generation claim per runSearch invocation, dead didSearchPaths removal, honest delivered-match cap through the #303 voice

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: runSearch claims the generation exactly once at invocation entry — `const generation = ++this._searchGeneration` moves above the empty-roots early return and the claim at :178 is removed — so every path (no opened roots, empty keyword, invalid max file size, dispatch) shares one claim per invocation and no completion belonging to a prior generation can write results, partialResults, running or activeCancel after any supersede; the early-return reset paths clear partialResults alongside results (the empty-roots and invalid-size paths already do; the empty-keyword path gains it so a cleared query cannot leave a stale partial notice beside an empty list); cancelRunning, #303's quiet-cancel semantics, the keystroke guard, the root-close defense-in-depth live-roots filter and the raw-promise activeCancel seam stay unchanged.

The didSearchPaths branch (:196-202) and the hardcoded "Showing first 100 results only" string are deleted — the store passes didMatch and didComplete only, with the option set otherwise unchanged; ripgrepSearcher's dormant 'searchedPaths' dispatch case and the dead typed facade ipc/runtime/search.ts stay read-only documented dead-parallel (no backend, wire or shim edit).

The honest delivered-match cap: one named documented module constant `const SEARCH_RESULT_CAP = 100` preserving the previous promise's number, counted on delivered matches — the grouped envelopes' matches summed, the same unit the overlay's resultSummary reports; a per-run capReached flag is set synchronously in the run's own didMatch path: envelopes are collected until the cap, the crossing envelope is sliced to the exact remaining count (SEARCH_RESULT_CAP total, never a zero-match entry, later envelopes dropped), and the in-flight walk is cancelled through the existing raw-promise cancel seam (the searchPromise.cancel closure — the same seam the dead branch used; no new canceller machinery, no generation bump); the run's .then writes `this.partialResults = terminalPartial || capReached` so the truncation never depends on the backend terminal and no capped set is ever presented as complete, while the error state stays empty — a cap is not a failure. File-local GRACE blocks updated: MODULE_CONTRACT SCOPE (supersede-on-every-path plus the delivered-match cap), MODULE_MAP, CHANGE_SUMMARY (LAST_CHANGE: C-SEARCH-LIFECYCLE-DISCARD), version comment bump.

Failing-first unload-cancel pins in tests/renderer/commands/quickOpen-deep.test.js: (a) with a controlled searcher walk in flight (mockSearchFn returning a deferred thenable whose cancel is a spy), unload() invokes the searcher cancel exactly once while subcommands still clear; (b) with the debounce pending (a controllable delay double replacing the module's resolved-promise mock), unload() cancels the pending timer (the delay double's cancel invoked) and clears _cancelFn; the existing "unload clears subcommands" pins (quickOpen.test.js :117, quickOpen-deep.test.js :373) stay green. Today unload only clears the list, so both new pins are red before the fix.

Implementation: unload keeps its existing contract (this.subcommands = []) and adds cancellation through the existing _cancelFn seam only — `if (this._cancelFn) { this._cancelFn() }` (the pending debounce timer or the active searcher promise; the search() self-supersede path is unchanged); the dead didSearchPaths branch (:139-147, the ">30 files" comment) is deleted — no didSearchPaths option is passed (the files-mode cost and cap design stays with C-QUICKOPEN-FILES-MODE); _doSearch keeps didMatch-only collection and its thenable resolve/reject shape; no debounce or searcher changes, no palette-side machinery.

Documented replacement of the three didSearchPaths-fed deep pins: :215 drops the options.didSearchPaths(1) call (didMatch-only); :242 "didSearchPaths sets canceled flag (< 30 does not cancel)" becomes a pin that the searcher options carry no didSearchPaths — the dead wire limit is removed; :282-296 drops the options.didSearchPaths(2) call keeping the didMatch-only result assertion; the file header line 13 ("_doSearch — didSearchPaths cancellation (numPathsFound > 30)") is rewritten to describe the removed option and the new unload-cancel coverage (review note (d)).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Failing-first palette stale-flash pins in tests/renderer/components/commandPalette-deep.test.js on the existing shallowMount + bus.on harness: with a currentCommand whose search returns controlled deferred promises — query A issued, query B issued, A's promise resolved first: A's resolution touches nothing (availableCommands does not flash A's list, searcherBusy and selectedCommandIndex are untouched) and B's resolution solely owns the list with searcherBusy false; a superseded rejection is dropped silently in both observed shapes — the factual cancel form `undefined` (delay().cancel() rejects with no argument, util/index.js :16 — review note (a); the spec's "message-null" phrasing describes the same silence guard, `error && error.message`) and a message-carrying rejection from a superseded request; the newest request's semantics are preserved unchanged, including the pinned silence for a message-less rejection of the current request (searcherBusy stays true — existing pin :439-459 stays byte-for-byte).

Implementation (script only): updateCommands captures a monotonic request sequence at entry — module-scope `let requestSeq`, `const seq = ++requestSeq` (the linkPathPicker seq precedent; equal consecutive queries still supersede because the sequence advances per request, not per query text) — and both the .then and .catch paths drop superseded settlements with `seq !== requestSeq` before any state write; the existing silence logic and comment for message-less rejections of the current request is preserved; handleDialogClose additionally resets searcherBusy to false with the other close resets — required because unload now actually cancels the in-flight request whose rejection lands silently and would otherwise strand the loading spinner into the next open; no template, layout, ARIA, placeholder or i18n change.

T-005.Title: Folder-close beats subscribe: watcher subscription identity in the project store

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Failing-first race test in tests/renderer/store/project.test.ts on the existing ipcWatchSubscribeMock seam (:80-90, the C-1/C-2 pins :283-305 stay green): ADD_PROJECT('/race') with a deferred subscribe promise, CLOSE_PROJECT('/race') arriving before the subscribe resolves, then the subscribe promise resolves with a spy disposer — the late .then invokes the disposer exactly once itself, the disposer map does not gain an entry for the closed root (nothing else ever calls the spy again), and a re-opened '/race' whose fresh subscription resolves while the root is open stores its own disposer, which a later CLOSE_PROJECT invokes exactly once while the stale disposer is never invoked a second time; a subscription resolving while the root is still open stores its disposer as before. Today the late .then stores a disposer for an already-closed root that nobody will ever call — the test is red before the fix.

Implementation: the pinned behavioral contract (after CLOSE_PROJECT no renderer listener for the closed root stays subscribed, no late .then stores a disposer for a closed root, a stale entry never overwrites a superseding subscription's disposer) is realized as a per-subscription token from one module-level monotonic counter plus a token map — ADD_PROJECT mints `const token = ++watchSubscriptionSeq` (a single module counter, never reset per root, so a closed-and-reopened root cannot collide with a stale in-flight subscription) and records it in a `watchTokens` Map before subscribing; the subscribe .then re-checks identity before storing — `watchTokens.get(canonical) !== token` means the root was closed or superseded, so the late .then disposes immediately and stores nothing; CLOSE_PROJECT keeps its synchronous dispose of stored disposers and the backend unwatch invoke unchanged, and additionally deletes the root's token-map entry together with the disposer entry (review note (c) — the token map itself is cleaned on CLOSE_PROJECT so the leak pattern is not reproduced); the ipcWatch facade (ipc/runtime/watch.ts) and the backend unwatch stay read-only.
